Subject: FintechCo - Logging controls & redaction (post-demo)

Thanks for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps on the logging/redaction items we discussed during the demo: 

Key ask summary:
- Confirm whether request/response logs (including headers and trace IDs) can be configured not to contain PII
- Data residency for logs: FintechCo needs EU-only storage for diagnostic logs and audit trails
- Retention: default 30 days, ability to set custom retention per-environment
- Ability to disable or minimize logging for specific routes that process sensitive PII

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Configurable redaction policies: full-body redact, field-level masking (JSON path), and header allowlist/denylist.
- Trace IDs: we can provide either unhashed trace IDs stored in secured logs or hashed/obfuscated IDs; mapping to internal request IDs can be restricted to KMS-protected stores.
- Data residency: for Dedicated/Private deployments we can ensure logs are stored in EU-only S3 buckets or customer-managed storage (VPC). Hosted customers can opt-in to EU-only logging where available.
- Retention controls: per-customer retention windows; we can set to 30 days by default and configure longer/shorter as required.
- No-request-logs option: for strict customers we support a mode where request payloads are never persisted; only minimal metadata for billing/metrics is retained.

Attached: redwood-logging-controls.pdf (concise config & examples).

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to prepare a short tech note with config examples and options (field masks, header lists, trace-id hashing).
2) We’ll share SOC2 evidence summary and the required compliance artifacts.
3) Schedule a 60-min tech deep dive next week with your infra/security engineer to review configuration and any gaps.

Can you confirm the EU-only requirement covers both request/response logs and audit logs? Also confirm whether FintechCo needs customer-managed storage (S3) or if a Redwood-hosted EU region is sufficient.

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A couple clarifying questions from our security team after the call: 

1) Redaction semantics: are the redactions applied server-side in the Redwood ingestion pipeline or do you offer client-side SDK hooks so we can mask at source? For compliance we'd prefer masking at client-side where feasible, but need server-side guarantees as a fallback.

2) Trace IDs: we’re concerned about correlation — does Redwood store a mapping table that ties trace IDs back to request metadata that could include PII? If so, can that mapping be disabled or kept encrypted with customer KMS?

3) Data residency & storage: FintechCo requires EU-only storage for all logs and diagnostic data. We need confirmation whether Redwood-hosted EU regions meet this or if we must use a private S3 bucket in our account (customer-managed). Also, please confirm the tooling for key rotation and KMS integration.

4) Retention: target 30 days for diagnostic logs, but we may need a 90-day retention for audit logs. Can you support separate retention policies for diagnostic vs audit logs?

5) We’re attaching our security questionnaire — can you point us to the artifacts you’ll share (SOC2 summary, logging architecture diagram, sample config)?

If you can send the tech note + SOC2 summary before our infra deep dive, that would help our scheduling.

Looping in technical details to answer Sasha’s questions — feel free to pull from this in the reply.

Summary answers:
- Where redaction happens: both. We support client-side SDK masking hooks (recommended for highest assurance) and server-side ingestion policies that apply JSON-path based masks and header denylists. Server-side redaction happens in the ingestion layer before any persistent storage is written.
- Trace ID handling: by default we emit an opaque trace_id for request correlation. We do NOT persist PII in mapping tables by default. If a customer requests full mapping (to support deep debugging), that mapping can be stored in a KMS-encrypted store and access-limited to a small set of roles. Alternatively we support storing only a hashed trace_id (SHA256 with salt) so you can correlate sessions without reversible identifiers.
- Data residency:
  - Hosted: we can enable EU-region logging for hosted customers where available, but retention and export controls are limited compared to Dedicated/Private.
  - Dedicated/Private: logs can be written to customer-managed S3 in your EU account (recommended for FintechCo) or to Redwood-managed buckets restricted to EU regions.
- Retention: yes — we support independent retention windows for diagnostic vs audit logs. Diagnostic defaults to 30d, audit can be 90d+.
- No-request-logs mode: supported. When enabled request bodies are not persisted; only metadata (timestamp, route, status code) is kept for metrics/billing.

Sample config (example ingestion policy):

"ingestion_policy": "{
  \"redact_fields\": [\"$.payment_card.number\", \"$.user.ssn\"],
  \"header_allowlist\": [\"content-type\", \"x-request-id\"],
  \"trace_id_mode\": \"hashed\",
  \"store_logs_in_customer_bucket\": true,
  \"customer_bucket_region\": \"eu-central-1\",
  \"retention\": {\"diagnostic_days\": 30, \"audit_days\": 90}
}"

Notes: the above is illustrative — we’ll provide a downloadable YAML/TOML snippet that your infra team can drop into their config.
